ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Srinivasa Ramanujan

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a cold with fever, and the question of an abscess relapse

text.paragraph: Sore throat, runny nose and cough for three days, and worry that the liver infection has come back. [S]

Mr. Ramanujan called this morning and was seen the same day. Three days ago he developed a sore throat, then a runny nose, sneezing and a dry cough; last night his temperature was 37.9 °C. Two students in his seminar have had colds this week. He has had no pain under the right ribs, no night sweats, no loss of appetite and no diarrhea, and his weight is still rising. He was frightened that the fever meant the abscess had returned and asked to be checked. He is in his third week of rifampin and taking it each morning; his urine and tears are orange, as he was told they would be, and he has had no nausea, rash or yellowing of the eyes. He is still going to counseling each week. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well, a little tired; temperature 37.8 °C, pulse 88, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Pharynx mildly red without exudate; nasal mucosa swollen; tympanic membranes normal
Clear on both sides, including the right base
Liver not tender or enlarged; no tenderness over the right lower ribs
Evening fevers to 38.6 °C with night sweats for about four weeks
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Weight loss of 5 kg over two months (57 to 52 kg), with poor appetite
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Dull right upper quadrant pain for three weeks, worse on deep breathing and lying on the right side, with a tender liver edge
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Amebic liver abscess: a single 6.2 x 5.4 cm abscess in the right lobe (segment VII) on ultrasound, Entamoeba histolytica antibody positive, blood cultures negative, years after two episodes of dysentery in India; treated with metronidazole and then paromomycin; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the hepatic amoebiasis later proposed for his illness
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; it does not settle the historical diagnostic conflict (CLM-0010, CLM-0011).
Vitamin B12 deficiency from a strict vegetarian diet (B12 168 pg/mL), with anemia (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 99 fL) to which inflammation also contributes
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
Positive interferon-gamma release assay, with chest radiograph and sputum smears and NAAT negative for tuberculosis; cultures pending
S — Synthetic finding, superseded by the diagnosis of latent infection when cultures were negative.
Latent tuberculosis infection: positive interferon-gamma release assay, normal lungs on the radiograph, three sputum smears, NAAT and cultures negative; treated with four months of rifampin
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; active tuberculosis was excluded, which does not settle the historical question.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (PHQ-9 12, no thoughts of self-harm) during a serious illness, far from his wife and family
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented loneliness; not a claim about his real mental health.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection, three weeks into rifampin and six weeks after treatment of the liver abscess, without signs of abscess relapse; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Viral upper respiratory infection (J06.9). A cold with a low fever, from contacts in his seminar. No sign of a relapse of the liver abscess: no right upper quadrant or rib tenderness, no night sweats, weight rising, white count 7.4, alkaline phosphatase 104 U/L, and a CRP of 11 mg/L, far below 92 at diagnosis and in keeping with a cold. A repeat ultrasound is not needed. No antibiotic is indicated. [S]
Rest, fluids, warm salt-water gargles and honey in warm water.
Acetaminophen up to 3 g a day for fever or sore throat.
Return or call for fever lasting more than three days, pain under the right ribs, breathlessness or blood in the sputum.

Latent tuberculosis infection on rifampin (Z22.7). Week three of four months: taking every dose; no nausea, rash or jaundice; ALT 32 U/L. Orange body fluids are expected. A cold does not change treatment. [S]
Continue rifampin 600 mg each morning.
Next clinical check at the preventive visit in three weeks.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). PHQ-9 7, improving. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline are in his phone. The fear of relapse was discussed and the results explained to him. [S]
Continue weekly counseling.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Guidelines for the Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection: Recommendations from the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association and CDC, 2020 (2020); DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024)

Follow-up: Call for fever beyond three days, right upper quadrant pain or breathlessness. Preventive visit in three weeks as booked. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-06: periodic adult preventive visit with pre-travel advice. [S]
